[cheerful] New lesson: comparing rows of the same table.

Link a table to itself to compare or pair its own rows.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] At the warehouse, the logistics team wants to combine the parcels of the same customer.

If a customer places two orders on the same day, a single parcel is enough.

To spot them, we get all the orders from the orders table.

For each one, customer underscore ID gives the customer and order underscore date the date.

Sophie Martin, customer 1, placed orders number 1 and number 2 on July 2.

Her order number 13, placed on July 28, will go in another parcel.

So we need to compare the orders with each other: same customer, same day.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] A self join is an ordinary join: the same table is read twice.

Each copy gets an alias: c1 for the first order, c2 for the second.

ON pairs two orders from the same customer, while the and keyword adds a condition: the same date.

Order number 1 has the same customer as number 1, number 2 and number 13…

…but number 13 was placed on July 28: it isn’t paired with number 1.

Number 2 is paired with number 1 and number 2, and number 13 only with itself.
